proof_summary: Prime-adic bounds, obtained by counting multiples of \(d=\operatorname{ord}_p(2)\) among the exponents and comparing with Legendre’s factorial valuation, show that any odd prime divisor \(p\) of a composite \(n\) divides \(a(n-1)\); the assumed divisibility would then force \(p\mid 2^{n-2}\), a contradiction. Powers \(n=2^r\) are excluded by the exact value \(v_2(a(2^r-1))=r-1\), while for prime \(n\), a proper order \(d<n-1\) makes the factor \(2^d-1\) force the same contradiction, so \(2\) has full order.
